lines.en: You keep looking at the door, Lola. Are you waiting for someone?
lines.pt: Você não para de olhar para a porta, Lola. Está esperando alguém?

lines.en: Yes, my new coworker, Jordan. We’ve only talked online, so I don’t know his face.
lines.pt: Sim, meu novo colega, o Jordan. Só conversamos online, então não conheço o rosto dele.

lines.en: Oh no! **What does he look like?** I can help you find him.
lines.pt: Ai, não! Como ele é? Posso ajudar você a encontrá-lo.

lines.en: **He’s tall** and thin, with short curly hair. **He has** glasses, too.
lines.pt: Ele é alto e magro, com cabelo curto e cacheado. Ele também usa óculos.

lines.en: Is that him, next to the window? **He looks** a little nervous.
lines.pt: É ele, ao lado da janela? Ele parece um pouco nervoso.

lines.en: Yes! He’s wearing a green jacket, just like he said he would.
lines.pt: Sim! Ele está de jaqueta verde, como disse que estaria.
E como ele é como pessoa?

lines.en: He’s really **friendly** and funny. Everyone in the office likes him.
lines.pt: Ele é muito simpático e engraçado. Todo mundo no escritório gosta dele.

lines.en: Then go say hi! I’ll keep your table. Don’t worry, **he looks nice.**
lines.pt: Então vá cumprimentar! Eu guardo a sua mesa. Não se preocupe, ele parece legal.

pages.title: Describing Someone You Are Meeting

situation.text: You are in a café waiting to meet someone you have never seen in person. A friend offers to help, so you describe the person: how they look and what they are like.

pages.goal: By the end of the class you can describe a person’s height, hair and clothes, say what they are like and ask for a description — politely and clearly.
canDo: Describe looks: He’s tall / She has curly hair
Ask for a description: What does he look like?
Describe personality: She’s friendly / He’s funny
Describe how someone seems: He looks nervous
success: I describe how the person looks.
I say what the person is like.
I ask a question about a person.
I avoid rude or too personal comments.
pages.think: When you describe someone in Portuguese, what do you mention first: the face, the clothes or the personality? Is it the same in English?

teach.goal: Abrir a aula pela situação real, não pela regra.
solo: Leia o objetivo e peça que o estudante diga, com as próprias palavras, o que vai conseguir fazer hoje.
Faça a pergunta “Think about it” antes de mostrar qualquer expressão.
group: Cada estudante diz uma palavra ou ideia que associa à situação.
Mostre os critérios de sucesso: eles são a missão final da aula.
support: Aceite respostas curtas ou em português na primeira rodada e reformule em inglês.

pages.title: Connection & warm-up

intro.solo: Start with real questions about the student’s life, not a grammar test.
intro.group: One question per student, then a follow-up question to a classmate.

pages.recall: Last weekend: “I visited… / It was…”. Ask: Who did you see last weekend? What was that person like?

qs.q: Who is the funniest person you know?
qs.pt: Quem é a pessoa mais engraçada que você conhece?

qs.q: Do you look like anyone in your family?
qs.pt: Você se parece com alguém da sua família?

qs.q: Have you ever met someone you only knew online?
qs.pt: Você já conheceu pessoalmente alguém que só conhecia online?

pages.tip: Use the answers to find gaps and to recycle earlier content. The goal is to enter English from the first minute.

teach.goal: Entrar no idioma no primeiro minuto e mapear lacunas.
extra: Who do you look like in your family?
How would a friend describe you?

errors.w: I look like my mother, she is tall (look/look like)
errors.r: I look like my mother. / She’s tall.

support: Ofereça as respostas-modelo (chips) e peça apenas que escolham uma e a ampliem com um motivo.

pages.title: Cultural snapshot — Polite descriptions
pages.intro: In the USA, describing people has unwritten rules: people usually mention hair, height and clothes, and avoid comments about weight, age or skin. Look and guess before you read.

cards.note: Neutral details that help someone recognize a person.
This asks for looks. “What’s he like?” asks for personality.
Personality words are usually positive in first descriptions.

qs.q: What do people mention to help you spot someone?
qs.pt: O que as pessoas mencionam para ajudar você a reconhecer alguém?

levels.A2: They say height, hair and clothes.
levels.B1: They give neutral details: height, hair, glasses and what the person is wearing.
levels.B2: They choose observable, neutral details, because clothes and hair help most and are not sensitive.

qs.q: Is it polite to say “He’s fat” or “She’s old”?
qs.pt: É educado dizer “He’s fat” ou “She’s old”?

levels.B1: No. Comments about weight or age can sound rude, so people avoid them or soften them.
levels.B2: Such comments are usually avoided with strangers; people prefer neutral or softer wording, such as “heavyset” or “older”, and only when really necessary.

qs.q: What is the difference between “look like” and “be like”?
qs.pt: Qual a diferença entre “look like” e “be like”?

levels.A2: “Look like” is for appearance; “be like” is for personality.
levels.B1: What does she look like? asks about appearance; What’s she like? asks about character.
levels.B2: The two questions share most words but ask different things; confusing them is a common learner mistake.

pages.compare: In Brazil people often joke about weight or looks among friends. In the USA, with people you do not know well, these comments are usually avoided. What feels normal where you live?

teach.goal: Ativar o contexto cultural e as primeiras hipóteses.
solo: Mostre os cartões e peça hipóteses antes de explicar.
Peça que compare com o que acontece no Brasil.
group: Cada estudante escolhe um cartão e explica em uma frase.
Pergunte “Do you agree?” entre colegas.
answers: Q3: look like = aparência; be like = personalidade.
extra: What do you notice first about a person?
Is there a description you would never say to a stranger?
support: Use as respostas de nível A1 como andaime e peça que repitam.
stretch: B2: compare o registro e o tom entre Brasil e EUA com exemplos reais.

pass1.pt: Por que a Lola descreve o Jordan?
opts: She is waiting to meet him
She wants to buy him a gift

teach.goal: Compreender a situação antes de ver o texto: ideia principal e depois informações específicas.
solo: Esconda o texto. 1ª escuta: só a ideia principal.
2ª escuta: peça os detalhes pedidos nas tarefas. Só depois mostre o texto.
group: Escuta coletiva; duplas anotam antes de revelar.
Compare as respostas entre duplas e só então mostre o texto.
answers: Pass 1: She is waiting to meet him
Pass 2: tall · curly · glasses · green jacket · friendly
extra: What does Will think of Jordan at the end?
Which detail helps most to find Jordan?
support: Pause depois de cada fala se necessário.

qs.q: What does Will say at the end?

retell.prompt: Retell the conversation in your own words, at your level.

teach.goal: Ler o diálogo, perceber os chunks e recontar.
solo: O estudante lê um papel e você lê o outro; depois troquem.
Peça que reconte a conversa no nível que conseguir.
group: Leitura em duplas e troca de papéis.
Reconto em cadeia: uma frase por estudante.
answers: In Lola’s office · Tall with curly hair · A little nervous · Jordan looks nice
extra: How would you describe the person next to you?
What would you ask to recognize a stranger?
support: Mostre a tradução (botão PT) depois da 2ª leitura.

pages.title: Useful expressions

items.pt: Ele é alto / Ela é baixa.

items.use: Say hair, eyes or glasses with have.
Say how someone seems right now.
Say what someone has on right now.
Be careful when you do not know.

pages.note: Instead of memorizing the whole list, choose 3–5 expressions (★) to use again and again. The others are for understanding and for stretching later.

teach.goal: Escolher 3–5 chunks para uso repetido e descobrir a função de cada um.
solo: Pergunte “When do you say it?” antes de dar o significado.
Compare formal × informal e peça um exemplo próprio.
group: Cada estudante escolhe a expressão que mais usaria e explica quando.
Comparem equivalentes em duplas.
answers: Asking for looks · Describing height · Hair and glasses · How someone seems · Personality
extra: Which expression helps you most in a hurry?
How can you soften a negative description?

errors.r: He has curly hair. / He’s got curly hair.
She’s a friendly person. / She’s friendly.

support: Trabalhe só as expressões ★ nesta aula.

head: Spoken English
Written English
register.note: In informal speech, He’s got is very common; both forms are correct.

teach.goal: Fixar os padrões principais (01 e 02); os outros são expansão. Usar a troca de palavras para variar a fala.
solo: Mostre o padrão DENTRO do diálogo (grife os chunks).
Use “Swap the words”: toque em cada peça e peça que o estudante diga a frase completa.
Compare spoken × written em 2 exemplos.
group: Troca em cadeia: cada estudante muda UMA peça e o próximo repete a frase.
Em pares: um escolhe as peças, o outro fala.
teach.answers: Padrões 01 e 02 são o foco; 03 e 04 são expansão para quem avançar rápido.
extra: Describe someone in this room in two sentences.
Change one adjective and read again.
support: Fique só com o padrão 01 na primeira rodada.
stretch: Combine dois padrões na mesma resposta.

pages.title: Pronunciation lab — natural American English
pages.tip: In English, the strong syllable carries the meaning: FRIENDly, CURly, NERvous. Stress it and say the other syllables weakly.

own.prompt: Write a true sentence describing a person you know with two adjectives.
own.criteria: Say it twice. Is the first syllable of each adjective stronger?

teach.goal: UM só fenômeno de pronúncia: Word stress in adjectives.
solo: 3 passagens: escutar e identificar, reproduzir ritmo e entonação, usar em frase com conteúdo próprio.
Modele devagar e em velocidade normal; peça que bata palmas na sílaba forte.
group: Coro, depois duplas; circule ouvindo.
Cada estudante cria uma frase própria usando o fenômeno.
answers: Identify: He’s friendly. · She looks nervous.
extra: Which adjective is hardest to stress?
support: Reduza a velocidade e conte as batidas em voz alta.

levels.h: Controlled practice — choose the best answer

items.q: 1. You want to know what a stranger looks like.
items.why: What does + subject + look like? asks for appearance.

items.q: 2. You want to know a person’s personality.
items.why: What’s she like? asks about character.
Use has with he/she for features.

items.q: 4. Your friend is yawning. What do you say?
items.why: look + adjective for how someone seems.

levels.h: Guided practice — complete, substitute and transform

items.why: Wearing for right now: is wearing.
look + adjective says how someone seems.

items.instr: Turn it into a question about appearance:
ans: What does your cousin look like?
What does your cousin look like
items.model: What does your cousin look like?

items.why: What’s … like? asks about personality, so answer with character.

teach.goal: Do controlado ao guiado: escolher, completar, substituir e responder antes da fala livre.
solo: Peça que o estudante justifique cada resposta.
Se acertar rápido, peça uma versão mais informal ou mais educada.
group: Resolvam em duplas e comparem antes de revelar.
Equipes: ponto por resposta justificada.
answers: What does he look like? · What’s she like? · He has curly hair. · You look tired. · has · is · He looks nervous. · What does your cousin look like? · She’s patient and really funny.
extra: Say each correct answer aloud and stress the adjective.
support: Ofereça o banco de palavras (chips) nas lacunas.

pages.title: Personalized roleplay — find the person

brief.teacher: You are a friend who will help find a person. Ask questions and confuse the student with a wrong guess.
brief.student: You are waiting for someone you have never met. Describe them so your friend can find them.

orders: A new coworker you have never met
A friend’s cousin arriving at the station
A new classmate who is late
complications: Two people look similar: add one more detail.
The friend points to the wrong person: correct politely.
You forget a word (curly, glasses…): describe it another way.
The friend asks what the person is like.
success: I describe how the person looks.
I say what the person is like.
I ask a question about a person.
I avoid rude or too personal comments.

teach.goal: Simulação com complicação inesperada e três rodadas com menos apoio.
solo: Combine o cenário com a vida real do estudante.
Rodada 1: com chunks. Rodada 2: só palavras-chave. Rodada 3: sem roteiro.
Meta de fala: 60–70% do tempo para o estudante. Anote 2–3 correções para a devolutiva.
extra: What if the other person asks for more detail?

errors.r: He wears glasses. / He has glasses.

support: Volte à rodada 1 se travar; peça que repita só a primeira frase.
stretch: Acrescente uma segunda complicação no meio da cena.

rounds.title: Describe
rounds.task: Describe a classmate or a celebrity without saying the name. Your partner guesses.

rounds.title: Ask
rounds.task: Ask three questions to find the mystery person.
rounds.hint: What does she look like? / Is she tall?

rounds.title: Personality
rounds.task: Describe a real friend: how they look and what they are like.

rounds.title: Group guess
rounds.task: Whole group: one pair describes, everybody else guesses.

infogap.title: Who is Sam?
infogap.instr: Ask your partner and complete your card. Do not look at the other card!

a.title: Description card A
a.task: You know how Sam looks. Ask your partner what Sam is like and what Sam is wearing.

b.title: Description card B
b.task: You know Sam’s personality and clothes. Ask your partner about Sam’s height and hair.

teach.goal: Fluência por repetição da função com informações novas a cada rodada.
group: Troque os pares a cada rodada (A+B / C+D → A+C / B+D → A+D / B+C → grupo todo).
Responsabilidade individual: cada aluno faz ≥1 pergunta e ≥1 resposta.
Circule anotando 2–3 correções prioritárias.
answers: A sabe: tall · short and curly. B sabe: shy but kind · a yellow raincoat. Perguntas: What does Sam look like? What’s Sam like? What’s Sam wearing?
support: Entregue frases-modelo no chat da turma.

pages.title: Group mission — find your contact
pages.goal: Each group must help a person recognize someone in a crowded place, using a clear and polite description.

missions.mission: One friend describes a cousin arriving from another city; the other tries to spot the cousin.
missions.start: My cousin is arriving at 5. She’s…

missions.mission: Describe your new manager to a colleague and say what he or she is like.
missions.constraint: Use “What’s he like?” and one personality adjective.
missions.start: Have you met our new manager?

missions.mission: A child is lost; describe the child to a teacher in a calm and clear way.
missions.constraint: Use “is wearing” and give three details.
missions.start: Excuse me, I’m looking for my son…

success: I describe how the person looks.
I say what the person is like.
I ask a question about a person.
I avoid rude or too personal comments.

teach.goal: Realizar algo com o inglês: o objetivo é resolver, não só falar certo.
group: Cada grupo recebe papel, restrição e missão. Alterne os papéis.
Progressão: 1ª rodada com frases de apoio, 2ª só palavras-chave, 3ª sem roteiro.
Observe e anote 2–3 correções prioritárias; devolutiva no fim.
answers: Modelo: “What does she look like?” → “She’s tall, with long straight hair, and she’s wearing a red coat.”
support: Dê o início de frase (“Start with”) em cada cartão.

pages.title: Writing — a small real-life task
pages.task: Write a short message to a friend who is going to pick up a guest at the airport. Describe the guest so your friend can recognize them.
pages.model: Hi Will! Thanks for picking up my cousin Carla. **She’s tall** and thin, **with long straight hair.** **She has** a big blue suitcase and **she’s wearing** a yellow coat. **She’s very friendly,** so just say hi. Thank you!
checklist: I used has/have for a feature.
I said what the person is wearing.
pages.tip: Fix only 2–3 priority points. Show a more natural way to say the same idea instead of rewriting everything.

teach.goal: Produção escrita curta ligada à situação comunicativa.
solo: Peça o texto; corrija 2–3 pontos prioritários e mostre uma forma mais natural.
group: Cada estudante escreve; depois troquem os textos e corrijam em duplas.
extra: Add one more detail about clothes.

errors.r: She has a yellow coat. / She’s wearing a yellow coat.

support: Dê o modelo e peça só para trocar os dados.

criteria.name: Fluency
criteria.desc: Mantém a comunicação sem interrupções excessivas.

criteria.name: Language use
criteria.desc: Utiliza adequadamente padrões, vocabulário e expressões.

criteria.name: Pronunciation
criteria.desc: É compreensível e usa ritmo e entonação adequados.

criteria.name: Interaction
criteria.desc: Responde, pergunta, esclarece e desenvolve a conversa.

interpret.text: Needs more support. Revisit the main patterns with guided practice before the next lesson.
Functional performance. Work on the lowest criteria in the next lesson.
Good control. Raise complexity and speed; add follow-up questions.
Strong performance. Move to a more demanding situation.

prompts.well: Example: You gave three neutral details so we could picture the person.
prompts.improve: Example: Use has with he/she (She has, not She have).
prompts.next: Example: Describe two people at once and compare them.

teach.goal: Avaliar o que o aluno conseguiu comunicar, não só os erros gramaticais.
solo: O estudante se autoavalia primeiro; depois você.
Feche com os três blocos: What you did well · What to improve · Your next challenge.
group: Dê um comentário por critério a cada estudante.
Cada um escolhe o próprio próximo desafio.
teach.answers: A rubrica é uma ferramenta interna de acompanhamento, não uma certificação CEFR.

tasks.name: Build a question
tasks.prompt: Without notes: ask what a friend’s cousin looks like.
tasks.model: What does your cousin look like?

tasks.name: Respond to a situation
tasks.prompt: A friend asks: “What’s your boss like?” She is kind.

items: Record a 45–60 second audio describing a family member.
Write four sentences describing a person in a photo.
Collect ten adjectives for looks and ten for personality.
Listen to the dialogue again and mark every use of has/is/looks.

unit: Tell · describe · compare · book · opine · advise · plan

teach.goal: Toda aula termina com uma produção observável.
solo: Sem consultar as anotações: construir uma pergunta, responder a uma situação e usar uma expressão nova.
group: Exit challenge individual; compare com o colega e combine a tarefa de continuidade.
answers: What does your cousin look like? · She’s kind and very organized. · He looks tired.
extra: Revisão espaçada: retomar descrições na aula 78 (missão integrada).

pages.title: Level up — the same situation from A1 to C2
pages.intro: You do not need six different methods: the structure stays, while language complexity and autonomy grow.

ladder.say: She is tall. She has a bag.
ladder.goal: Say simple facts about a person with models.

ladder.say: He’s tall and thin, with curly hair, and he’s wearing a green jacket.
ladder.goal: Describe looks and personality with several details.

ladder.say: He’s kind of shy at first, but once you talk to him he’s really easygoing.
She comes across as reserved, though she’s actually very warm once you get to know her.
He has a rather understated charm that grows on you, and he never seems to want the spotlight.
There’s a quiet authority about her, the kind that doesn’t need to announce itself.

pages.note: This progression is illustrative: complex sentences do not define a level on their own. CEFR also considers comprehension, autonomy, fluency, accuracy, interaction and appropriateness.

teach.goal: Mostrar a progressão sem criar seis metodologias.
solo: Mostre onde o estudante está e a próxima etapa.
group: Cada um escolhe a frase do próprio nível e a do próximo.
extra: Which sentence would you like to be able to say next month?
